utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is the Defence ready to continue the examination-in-chief of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Usher, please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the meantime, I should like to have placed on the ELMO the same map that we had before, but the usher is not available for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the Registrar, it is the map referring to incident number 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. DP16.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you have given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony, yes. Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was asking that we place on the ELMO, yes, thank you. Maybe I wasn't heard. The map referring to incident number 20. Exhibit 3834. I would also like to have placed 3268, Exhibit 3268 on the ELMO, as well. It's an exhibit that has been tendered under seal. Therefore, the necessary measures need to be taken to protect the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will turn into private session for that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You told us something yesterday with respect to point number 10, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I should like to summarise what you said yesterday, that is that point 10 could not be seen from the lines. I am now asking you the same question, Witness, with respect to point number 7. Could point number 7 be seen? Was it visible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As that is a high-rise building, it has at least six or seven floors and there are buildings of equal height in front of it, it is very difficult to be seen, but I don't believe it can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, with the assistance of Madam Registrar, could you place Exhibit 3268 on the ELMO, ERN 4325, the second photograph, please. But we need to protect it -- no. All names need to be concealed, so with a post-it on it, I think, at least, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... like to see before putting it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you see here a view of a part of Sarajevo. Do you recognise this area and this street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What is the main road that we see on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ivana Krndelja Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, would you point -- look at the centre of this photograph, and according to your knowledge of the place, could you tell us roughly from which spot this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just above the transit, behind the Zeljeznicar stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you think that this photograph was taken from the VRS lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suggest we remove the photograph from the ELMO with the assistance of the usher, and that we place once again the map that we had a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, will you please focus now on point 27 appearing on this map. Could you point it out, please. This red dot.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which number did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Twenty-seven.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see a 27.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you enlarge a view of this map, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the witness is pointing to number 27 on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, according to your knowledge of the area, that is not only the existence of the hill and the town at the foot of it, was it technically possible to hit point 27 from one or other of the three red circles that you referred to on this map; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you explain to this Chamber briefly why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, there are two reasons, actually. The distance is certainly greater than 1.000 metres; and secondly, the configuration of the ground and the separation line is such that that point is not visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say that it is not visible, there must be several reasons for this, a point is not visible because it is too far away, for instance, or it's not visible because there is something that is obstructing the view or some other reason. So what is the reason that you are saying that this point was not visible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said that the configuration of the land was the reason, also the separation line between the VRS and the BH Army on the ground marked here with red circles is either flat or sloping downwards towards the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And that would be your answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I should also like you to look now at point 15 indicating it, pointing it out so that we are sure that you have seen it. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the witness does so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Regarding this point 15 and more specifically the circle furthest to the right which I would be grateful if you could find to the right of number 90, and also with regard to the -- all the other points within a perimeter corresponding to number 154, regarding the towers that you have identified.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was it possible, technically, to have a line of fire from these points to point number 15; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the position S, no. From position 154, partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say "position S" you pointed to the circle next to number 90, and then you pointed to the buildings under 154. Why are you saying partially? You are not getting the translation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I didn't get it right away. I didn't get your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Excuse me. Let me repeat: Why, the area referred to as 154, did you say it was possible partially?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we see in front with the number 217 written on it, I said that that was a football stadium. Its height determines the possibility of having a broader view from position 154.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. You said one could have a partial line of fire. I still haven't seen your answer. Between point 15 and the group with buildings 154, was it possible, according to you, to hit this point which is situated before -- behind the buildings? Was it physically possible to hit the ground from point 154?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not quite sure. On this map as it is depicted, it is impossible. The reason is that this northern side of the stadium consists of a concrete stalls which is 20 metres and more in height, and this building next to number 15 is in Ivo Lola Ribar Street I know also very well that building. It also obstructs point number 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, yesterday we said that you were granted 10 minutes. You are over that now, considerably.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Only a few more minutes. I would like another map to be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just in order to understand you well, "a few more" is certainly not more than five.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a photograph that I think it was also under seal, 3234. In the meantime, I will ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you redrew yesterday or partially redrew the line of the enemy, do you remember, in connection with incident number 15?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the incidence of combat in this area and their scope?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incidence of the exchange of fire was such that it was a daily occurrence, and the fighting was of lower intensity. The attacks by one side was of low intensity, yet fire was exchanged on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And which weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I was speaking of the frequency of combat and not of scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have that photograph placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Mr. DP16, you've told us that you fought with the Bosnian Serbian Army between September 1992 and August 1994. In that period did you have any other duties, apart from being a fighter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the last year of the war, in 1995, from the trenches, the front line, I went to the communication centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, you've mentioned certain communications involving the media. Was anyone from the corps command ever involved in your dealings with the media?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know a member of the Bosnian Serb Army by the name of

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met this man with the surname [redacted]after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you personally ever go to the corps command headquarters during the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- to avoid confusion of any kind, could one be more specific and say what the name of this man [redacted] was, so that we can know exactly who we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The person [redacted]you spoke about, what's his first name? Do you know that, Mr. DP16? You said you met him after the war, so you must have a specific person in mind. Could you tell us what is the first name of that person you had in mind when you answered that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I know that we should perhaps go into private session before you answer that question. But my first question is, do you know his first name? Don't mention it yet. Do you know his first name? Yes, then we will turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, the only question and you were expecting it, that was the question, but the name was mentioned before in relation with a communications network. I think that for the public, it would be very easy to connect these two matters and to find out -- and to find out who we are talking about. So I don't know whether the transcript, the prior transcript should be redacted. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [redacted] [redacted] is it any of them that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't -- I don't recall the pseudonym. Perhaps we could go into private session. I notice that we are not. I wish to make a submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, between September 1992 and August 1994, were you a member of the 1st Sarajevo Mechanised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a member of the 3rd Battalion, 3rd Company, and the name of the higher level unit, to tell you the truth, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that you changed companies to the Novo Sarajevo Chetnik detachment. When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, I'd ask that Mrs. Pilipovic keep her voice down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my apologies. Ms. Pilipovic didn't say a single word. I spoke, and as lowly as I could. I would like to check before making an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But please take off your earphones. It should become a routine so that we don't need any intervention from the Prosecution and we don't have any necessity to -- yes,

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I as we would like to save time, could I ask your Chamber and the Prosecution to wait. I have an objection to make. I wish to check on the transcript, because I cannot rely on the memory of Ms. Pilipovic. I wish to check on the transcript so would you be kind enough to wait a moment for me to check.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in order to save time which is precious, I will not search and I will rely on memory of Ms. Pilipovic that that was not quite the testimony of this witness who said that the company changed its name, it was re-named, rechristened or apparently I am mistaken. I'm sorry. I don't know. In that case, I withdraw the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: If there is any concern I can read the evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is withdrawn as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It took us quite some time, but I notice, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that you are talking it very seriously by even taking off your glasses and not just your headphones. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace, and may I urge the parties not unnecessarily to intervene. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- from the 3rd detachment of the 3rd Battalion, I moved to a company of the Novo Sarajevo Chetnik detachment in 1995.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises, didn't hear the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When about in 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in the spring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And not only did he say in the spring, but we are far beyond the time period of interest to us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ierace, the witness has answered the question so the question of relevance is not necessary to discuss at this very moment. Please proceed. But if you go beyond the time frame of the indictment, would you then please indicate what the relevance would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will, Mr. President. The English transcript didn't refer to spring.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was Slavko Aleksic your company commander between September 1992 and some stage in 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My commander, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Who was your company commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of my company in the 3rd Battalion the commander was Stanic, Mirko, I think, was his first name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: At any stage during the war was Slavko Aleksic your company commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was, when I joined that company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said in the spring of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, once again I will rephrase the same objection. We asked Mr. Ierace not to put questions beyond the relevant time period, and we come up against the same problem, time and time again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't think the question was about outside of the time frame, it was only in the answer that it turned out to be out of the time frame. And, of course, Mr. Ierace could not -- the question is not beyond the time frame. Please proceed, and may I urge again the parties, if it would happen that we hear a few words from outside the time frame, I think both parties have caused this to happen. The Chamber is well aware that whatever information it receives in evaluating it, that of course, it will keep a close eye on what is in the time frame and what is not in the time frame. So I urge the parties again not to unnecessarily interfere. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Before you joined his company or before he became your company commander, at any stage during the conflict did you see in the vicinity of the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How often between September 1992 and August 1994 would you see him in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, twice a week. And maybe even more frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What were the circumstances that you would see him at least twice a week?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were neighbours even before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do I take it that you are telling us that you would have contact with him because he was a friend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The fact that one is neighbours -- one was neighbours before the war, does not necessarily explain why you would see each other at least twice a week during the war. Apart from being neighbours, were you also friends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Before the war we never socialised privately, and during the war because of the circumstances we found ourselves in, we would meet once or twice a week and get together privately as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How many soldiers were there in your company in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know the exact number, but I can tell you approximately some 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did that number change in 1994 or did it remain approximately the same?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It changed drastically.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. When in 1994 did it change drastically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in 1994, but throughout the wartime period, from the first days of the war until the end, that number became smaller and smaller.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In 1993, how many different companies had responsibility for the Jewish cemetery part of the confrontation line? Just one or more than one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Jewish cemetery itself only one company, that is the 3rd Company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was Slavko Aleksic in your company in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: He wasn't in your company. Was he -- and yet having regard to your earlier answers, he was in the vicinity of the Jewish cemetery; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, above the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: He remained further to the south?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In 1993 did he have his own company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't his own company.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In 1993 was he a company commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. So he was the commander of the company which had responsibility for the front line next to yours, is that correct, in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How many members were there of his company in 1993, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, about 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did his company include any Russians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could describe his company as being an international one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Does that mean the answer is yes, there were Russians in his company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Hungarian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Korean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Korean, a Japanese, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were there members of his company who would join for short periods of time and then leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such people throughout the war who, due to the difficulties in the method of warfare, would leave the lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were there -- I withdraw that. You said that you could describe his company as being an international one. International volunteers would be an accurate description as well, wouldn't it, that is an individual who would travel to Sarajevo and join his company, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Some would come for just weekends, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Weren't there individuals who would travel from Serbia for a matter of a few days at a time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of a single such case within the territory of the area of responsibility of our battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that in order for individuals to travel to Sarajevo, that is, nationals from other states to travel to Sarajevo to fight, to put their life on the line, they must have felt passionately about the cause, do you agree with that? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Tell me what the term "Vojvoda" V-O-J-V-O-D-A means?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably in your own language you have the same title, Duke. In any event, in the Serbian language and for the Serb people the word "Vojvoda" means an honourable and honest man.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Does it have any connotations of leadership?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does have that connotation as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it a term that suggests a high degree of respect, that is the person is held in high esteem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in every sense of the word.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You told us that the detachment that you joined in 1995 was known as the Novo Sarajevo Chetnik detachment. What does Chetnik mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps this objection could be made in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will answer. I will answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is an objection and the court first has to decide on the objection, at least, once we have heard the objection. I would prefer to hear the objection in the absence of the -- yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the problem is the following: Is the question as put in a general sense, what does the word Chetnik mean, we accept it. If this question is attached to what happened in 1995, that is after the relevant time period, in that case we have an objection for purely chronological reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The question was put in a general sense and you indicated that you would like to answer the question. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The term Chetnik is of old Slavonik origin and it means a person in uniform, that is the original meaning. And if you wish me to give its second meaning, I can do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, please, tell us that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Serbian people as probably the only European nation that has this term, Chetnik, indicating a member of a military unit, a Chetnik implies a member of special units with full and complete training for the tasks assigned to it, and which implies heroism, courage and absolute compliance with all the rules of warfare.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could the term Chetnik be applied to someone of a Muslim background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could it be applied to someone of -- from the Croatian community?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if he is a member of units of the Serbian Army. The same applies to Muslims because they have their own names for that type of army, or unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What are the names which apply to persons of the Muslim faith that have a similar meaning or the same meaning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let us say "Mujahedin", for instance, as far as I know. Yes, "Mujahedin," yes. Or the jihad as a warrior.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And in relation to persons of Croatian backgrounds, what terms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our part of the world, the customary term of Croats, members of such units is Ustasha.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you understand from your evidence that Chetnik is the counterpart for persons who fight in the Serbian cause to Mujahedin in respect of Muslims, and Ustasha in respect of Croatians; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President. Objection based on semantics, each of these words should be understood within their relevant context, so there is never an equivalence, a member of an SAS could never be identical--

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think my learned colleague should be far more discerning on what he says in the presence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me rephrase this. The objection is linked to the semantic meaning and the placing of words into context.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I take the view that given the wording that my learned colleague chose, the question no longer is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact you asked the witness to confirm how you understood his answer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have heard his answer. The -- we'll have to do it with that. At the same time, if the Defence is concerned about the Chamber to, at best, understand the answers of the witnesses, then it might be useful not to intervene on these terms because we might miss something that could lead to a better understanding of the testimony of the witness. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the ELMO could be moved. It is difficult for me, sometimes to see the face of the witness with that machine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the map can be taken off the ELMO as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: A Chetnik, a person described as a Chetnik you told us is a soldier who fights with honour. Central to the notion is someone who fights passionately for the Serbian cause, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first place, bravely, and passionately has certain negative connotations that I as a member of those unit do not recognise or accept.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In terms of its general understanding, the term Chetnik denotes someone who is above everything else, a person who regards himself as a Serb, that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What you said a moment ago, when you said passionately, the term "passion" implies also hatred and bravely or heartedly does not imply hatred. Believe me, a Chetnik does not hate his enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. I did not use the term "passion" or "passionately" in my last question. I will repeat the question. In terms of its general understanding, the term Chetnik denotes someone who is above everything else, a person who regards himself as a Serb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not getting the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Neither am I, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I will just move to 6 and see whether we have translation again on 6. Could you please repeat your question. Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Would you rather the question be repeated and then my objection or can I do it now? Can I make my objection now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, of course, if I am aware that you want to make an objection, you will get an opportunity. It is not even necessary to raise your voice in that respect. Please -- could the objection be made in the presence of the witness? If not, we will have to ask him to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that it can be made in the presence of the witness and I don't think I raised my voice. I do apologise if that is the impression I gave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, what I wanted to say was that the second part of Mr. Ierace's question appears to be in contradiction with the reply given by his witness a moment ago, when he said "yes, a Muslim can be a member -- a Chetnik too." So this second part of the question is in contradiction with a previous answer of the witness, so that is the gist of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This objection is denied. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, what I am suggesting to you is that in the same way as the term "Mujahedin" denotes someone who is fiercely loyal or strongly loyal to their Muslim faith, apart from anything else, in the same way as the term "Ustasha" denotes someone who is strongly Croatian in their self-identity, so does the term "Chetnik," denotes someone who regards him or herself as a strong Serb nationalist; do you agree or do you disagree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I further suggest to you that the term Chetnik denotes someone who is not only a soldier, but a ferocious soldier, a fierce soldier. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you're adding the notion of passion which I do not accept as a member of those units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: We are talking generally, rather than in relation to those units, I remind you. Leaving the units aside or the unit, the Novo Sarajevo Chetnik detachment, and talking about one's understanding of the term, do you not agree that in summary a person who is a Chetnik is a fierce Serb nationalist soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Aleksic regarded himself as a Chetnik, didn't he, that is, Slavko Aleksic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Objection, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a question regarding the intimate nature of a third person of which the witness has said he was not his friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sometimes you can know something about the intimate feelings about someone, even if it is not your friend. But Mr. Ierace, perhaps it is better to ask this question in a more factual way. But again what I noticed at this moment is that the interventions are not always well-based, and they do interrupt the flow of information considerably. I have to urge the parties again to make it possible for each other to examine a witness. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In 19 -- I withdraw that. Between September 1992 and August 1994, did Slavko Aleksic have long hair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you have long hair in that same period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have had long hair for 30 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: One of the physical characteristics of a Chetnik is a person who has long hair and a beard; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I appreciate that that does not mean of course that everyone who has long here and a beard is a Chetnik, but simply that that is one of the symbols, the visual symbols of being a Chetnik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Most members of the Novo Sarajevo Chetnik detachment had short hair.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, again, you are taking my question as referring to that detachment. At this stage, I am not. We are talking about one's general understanding of the term Chetnik. Do you now agree that that is one of the symbols of being a Chetnik, having long hair and a beard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to make a comment with your permission, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not mind if you make a comment, but I'd like you first to answer the question. The question is more or less that whether the stereotype picture of a Chetnik would show him with long hair and a beard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Yes, the witness asked whether he was allowed to add something, but I asked him first to respond to the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That stereotype exists as a result of the end of the Second World War, that is, the arrival of the communists or rather socialism as a system within the territory of the former Yugoslavia. Such a stereotype does exist and it has led to -- the aesthetics that was accepted in those days was short hair. But the long hair in the Chetnik was the struggle of freedom. The moment a war ends and fighting ends, that same man has his hair cut. So the product of all these questions on the part of the Prosecution, refers to the connotation and the context of the relationship between the state toward certain detachments from the Second World War from the period of socialism in Yugoslavia, during the socialist period in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you've explained the stereotype of this but looking at the clock I know it is time for a break. We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with your permission we are well aware of the fact that long beards in fashion in a certain sense, but we don't want to waste too much time. We don't want to waste too much time on the history of Chetniks and to follow this line, because we really don't think that this is why we are here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber has heard your observations. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, are you ready to continue the cross-examination of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was Aleksic in 1993 known as Vojvoda Aleksic, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can we assume from that title that he commanded a great deal of respect amongst the Bosnian Serb soldiers in the vicinity of the Jewish cemetery between September 1992 and sometime in 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were there times when Aleksic's soldiers were moved for short periods to other parts of the confrontation lines around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Given this type of question, Mr. Ierace should be more precise with regard to the time concerned. Are we still dealing with the period between 1992 and 1994 or after this period?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the earlier question was about September 1992 and 1994, so it is not necessary to repeat that in every single question. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I urge to the parties not to intervene unnecessarily. This is the last warning. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the territory of Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Not just Grbavica, but other parts of the confrontation line around Sarajevo as well, any part?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, was that done because he and his soldiers were regarded as, let's say, particularly fierce soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Who did it, who gave the orders to move him and his soldiers from time to time to other parts of the confrontation lines? Where did those orders come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the younger soldiers from the territory where the Grbavica Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. line was went into the field to hold the lines in mountains such as Treskavica. Similarly, Vojvoda Aleksic's men went to carry out their duties as ordered by the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And between September 1992 and August 1994 who was or who were the battalion commanders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very beginning of the war until about the end of 1992, I really don't know the names of the battalion commanders, but I do know when -- I know of the commander's name when Blagoje Kovacevic came. That was at the end of 1992 or the beginning of 1993. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And he was the commander of your battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How long did he stay in that position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the time I mentioned, whether it was the end of 1992 or the beginning of 1993, and right up until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was there also a battalion commander by the name of Slobodan Aleksic, not necessary of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were you ever repositioned to other parts of the front lines between September 1992 and the end of 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Which other parts of the front lines were you deployed to in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the battlefield around Orlovo and the battlefield in the Treskavica mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In terms of morale of the -- your fellow soldiers, if morale was seen to be waning, if there was less of a will to fight aggressively, would Aleksic's troops be brought in at different parts of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was a breakthrough, if the defence line had been penetrated, then parts of his company would be taken to that line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And was that partly because he and his troops were regarded as having a particularly strong will to fight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of his unit consisted of men who were responsible for that kind of combat, that is to say for obtaining the lines, holding them as they were. That doesn't mean that they were particularly talented for fighting. That was their duty, and it is a duty that they accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, I don't think you've answered the question. What I am asking you is: Leaving aside matters of expertise and training, did they have a particularly strong spirit which was a reason, in part, for them to be moved when required to other parts of the confrontation line, a fighting spirit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To an extent, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Wasn't one of the problems that many of the members, many of the soldiers of the Bosnian-Serb Army who served in Sarajevo were locals and many of them did not particularly want to engage non-Serbs who had earlier been neighbours, wasn't that a problem?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is understandable that most people and most fighters weren't in favour of the war, but that wasn't their personal problem. War's a general phenomena, a general problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, it was particularly a problem for the commanders, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what my impression was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The Jewish cemetery was a particularly sensitive part of the front line between September 1992 and August 1994, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: One of the reasons it was so sensitive was because it afforded a view over the centre of the city at close quarters, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know if anyone is also listening to the French booth, but I do so occasionally. And the usher is requested to put on the second microphone, the witness's second microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you take care that the left microphone of the witness is switched on as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, you disagree with that. I suggest to you that the distance between the northern boundary of the Jewish cemetery and what you yesterday called the Marijn Dvor intersection, is around 460 metres; do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that that is the distance, more or less, but I don't agree that that is the reason for the intensity of the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What do you say was the reason for the intensity of the fighting at the Jewish cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, above all, there were mostly exchanges of fire and there was no movement on the Serbian side, not on a single occasion. And on the Muslim side that happened at least 10 times in the course of the war, and the intensity was great. That is why there was large-scale fighting there and fire was constantly being exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, you told us you have an explanation as to why that was a sensitive part of the front line and what you essentially told us is that the reason is that it was constantly under attack from the enemy forces. I suggest to you that the obvious reason why there was persistent fighting at that point, why that piece of territory was so sensitive and important was because of its proximity to the centre of the city and the view it afforded of the centre of the city; don't you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree that the town is visible from that position, the entire town, but I don't agree that that is the reason for the war or rather I think that you are insisting on the fact that it would have been better if the Serbs and their families had moved further into the depth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us that you knew Aleksic before the war. Did he have a criminal record?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not a policeman. I don't know about a record. As far as I know, no proceedings were instituted against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did he have a reputation for being a violent man before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As a neighbour, he was almost invisible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did an unusually large number of soldiers in his unit have criminal records dating back to before the war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, after some hesitation, I think that the rule says that if one party is examining with regard to certain issues, it has to verify whether the witness knows this himself. This ought to be applied now, all the more so, given that the witness just said that he knew nothing about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness answered the question in respect of Mr. Aleksic, and the question is now not about Mr. Aleksic any more. Do you have any knowledge on criminal records of members of the unit commanded by Mr. Aleksic that originate from before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the "international part of the unit," I know nothing, but for the other men who were people who lived in that area, I can claim for certain that they didn't have such records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You told us that from the cemetery one could see the city. That included the trams when they ran, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The trams themselves, only partially, only briefly. They were concealed behind the buildings. The buildings obstructed the vision. From the lines that were held by the Army of Republika Srpska, there was an obstruction of the view.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let me ask you a hypothetical question: If between September 1992 and August 1994 you observed, travelling on a tram, a group of armed soldiers from the enemy side, what you would call the enemy side, would you have shot them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the trams started working only in the summer of 1994, perhaps, so there was no need to think about this matter before Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that. And my personal answer would be, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why would you not have shot them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, above all because a tram is a civilian vehicle, and even if one assumes that soldiers might use it, one could assume that there are civilians in trams, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you have regarded your position as consistent with the orders you told us you received to the effect that you should respect civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: To the point that even if you were in a position to shoot a group of armed soldiers on a tram, out of respect for the possibility of inadvertently hitting civilians, you would have refrained from doing so; is that a fair statement of your position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President -- I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us that there were some barracks, I think, alongside the Jewish cemetery having regard to how you pointed them out on a map, and that those barracks were targeted by a tank; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: On how many separate occasions were the barracks targeted by a tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I myself know about two occasions took place at two separate intervals.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When were they, those two occasions, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The end of 1992 and in the course of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown Exhibit D1809.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please assist, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Does point number 10 that you marked indicate the position of the barracks? Is it 10 or is it --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now, if I understand the effect of your evidence yesterday, were you also stationed at about point number 10? Is that where you spent most of your time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, between 50 and 100 metres further to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you tell us briefly what the barracks looked like? Was it a brick building, a concrete building, just a ground floor or ground floor plus a storey or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building was made of bricks. It was probably an old building. I don't know exactly when it was built. It was a ground-floor building about 30 metres long and one could say that it was fairly small. It was one of the smaller barracks that the JNA had in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So it was used as barracks before the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was it your company commander's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was it Aleksic's headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you please point to where your company commander's headquarters were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the immediate vicinity of the first line, which, as I said, went down the Nevesinjska Street. There is the Travnicka Street there and that is where my company's command, the 3rd company, had its command before arriving in the Vojvodina unit, in the Vojvoda's unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you please take a pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Again I forget what the colour is. Is it black, blue?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And circle the position and place a letter "A" beside it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are referring to the command of my company?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you please with the letter "B" alongside it place a circle to indicate the position of Aleksic's headquarters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, you also told us that your orders to respect civilians were given every time you collected ammunition. Where did you collect your ammunition from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally never went to collect ammunition, but the people who were tasked to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Firstly, where did they collect it from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, from the barracks in Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you mean also the same complex, barracks in the same complex, which included the corps command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Who would bring your ammunition to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were people whose duty it was, the quartermasters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How frequently, let's say in 1993, would you receive fresh ammunition from the quartermaster?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The year 1993 was quite a peaceful year, so that during that year, very rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am sorry? Didn't you tell us that you were under attack on a daily basis throughout the period September 1992 to August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, in 1993 were you ever under attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So, in 1993 how often would you be re-equipped with ammunition by the quartermaster?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, that is a hypothetical question and it must be given a hypothetical answer. What I am able to recollect at this point in time is that I think it would be once in three months.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: As far as you know -- I withdraw that. Did Aleksic's company in 1993 receive their ammunition in the same fashion, that is, someone travelling to Lukavica to pick it up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of us received weapons in that way, that is ammunition, rather.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, I think yesterday you told us that you received those orders "every time when we had to go to fetch fresh ammunition and sometimes with greater frequency." Does that in fact mean only once every three months in 1993? Is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant that when these men went to fetch ammunition, they came back with the order. And the second part of my answer, that is even more frequently, meant always when anyone from the lower command came to visit the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you mean higher command or lower command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant lower-level officer who came to visit the lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you mean lower-level officers from Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Lower-level officers of --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officers of -- officers from the battalion command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know where the battalion headquarters were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please mark them on the map with the letter "C" and a circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might the witness now be shown Exhibit D18 -- I think it is 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please assist in showing the exhibit to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am sorry. Just before that map is taken away, just one more question in relation to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you see on the map the State Hospital? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please place a circle around it and the letter "D" and is it indicated by a cross on the map, a symbol of a cross; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, if we could change maps now. And to assist the usher, can we keep it focused on close quarters -- yes, thank you, that's fine. Perhaps we can centre the map on the cemetery. Place the cemetery more in the centre of the map, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: On this map you placed with a circle yesterday the position where you were stationed, is that correct, approximately being the small circle on the -- halfway along the western boundary of the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, I don't know whether you can see it, but there appear to be some symbols on the map further along that street. What appears to be some cross-hatching, yes. Were there any orchards or fields in the area of those symbols along that little street to the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, as far as the cemetery itself goes, did it have tombstones?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did it have trees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did it have a lot of trees or not so many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not so many.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: According to you, you were on the western side, the enemy was on the eastern side, were the trees damaged during the war, those that were there in no-man's land?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area that I am going to point to you, from this position here, as I have just shown you, that is where the -- the most of the trees were and it is understandable that due to constant opening of fire by both sides, those trees were damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: For the benefit of the transcript, the witness indicates the top, that is the northern half of the cemetery, in particular with the word "cemetery" appears.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that the chapel was a source of fire from the ABiH; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only the chapel, but also this eastern side, the eastern wall of the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How big was the chapel or how small, if you like, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I grew up there and I am very familiar with the chapel. On numerous occasions as a child I entered it. It was roughly the height of a normal four-storey buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What about the area of the ground that it took up, can you tell us in square metres, perhaps, or dimensions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could say that the dimensions were approximately 20 by 30 metres. 20 metres by 30 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say that it was four storeys high, did it have four storeys, or was that perhaps the height of the structure only?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had three storeys, for certain, that I went to, plus the dome of the chapel itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What type of fire did you receive from the chapel, apart from infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the chapel itself, nothing else was fired from except infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How far was the chapel from the road, approximately, the closest part of the chapel to the nearest part of the arterial road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A couple of metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And just to be clear on it, would you please point to the arterial road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates the thick yellow road passing, forming the northern boundary of the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That's correct, isn't it, the road forms the northern boundary of the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, actually the northern wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And if one walked from the road towards the chapel, would one be walking uphill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was that northern boundary about 100 metres long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I'd like to explain the kind of terrain it was. The entrance to the cemetery was at the level roughly of the second storey of the chapel. And you also entered the chapel going uphill, but here, this edge that I am showing you, just below this road there is a passage, and the entrance to the chapel is roughly here, a passage going under the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: A passage going under the road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: At that point, and I will describe it in a minute, was the second level of the chapel at ground level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in relation to the entrance to the cemetery, which was here. But the entrance to the chapel was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, where you first indicated the entrance to the chapel, you said approximately in the middle of the red circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, the other position, the other entrance.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the entrance to the cemetery, not the chapel, and then after you enter the cemetery, you could enter the higher storey of the chapel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now, I think you earlier indicated when you said the entrance to the chapel was under the road, slightly to the south of the intersection of the arterial road and the road forming the western, that is, the north-western boundary of the cemetery; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: People lived in this chapel, people who were maintaining the chapel and who were providing maintenance for the Jewish cemetery. And the entrance to their dwelling was from this subway that passes under the road and that is the entrance to their apartment and the entrance to the chapel is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please take a blue pen and draw as accurately as you can on the map, the walls of the chapel, its position in the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask the witness be shown an exhibit that might take a few moments to find it, Exhibit P3279-J. I think there are a number of photographs which are part of that exhibit. I would like the witness to see one and then another. The first photograph is marked 22-A.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, if one walked north from that part of the arterial road, would it ground drop suddenly away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was constantly dropping away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But at the road level there is something of a ledge as you look north; isn't that the case? You would be walking down steps or a steep slope if you went north from the arterial road; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And in terms of the area within the circle, were there any other buildings apart from the chapel either on the road level or to the south or was the chapel the only one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the road level there was just a checkpoint of the French units and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Before the war was there a garage in that area on the other side of the road or some similar building, elevated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was there a guardrail along that part of the arterial road because of the drop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was it a two-lane fairly major road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We called it the transit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So I take it the chapel was quite an irritation to you and your fellow soldiers being such a constant source of fire and being the only building in that area, either at road level or between your forces and the road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't know whether Madam Registrar has finished locating --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There seems to be some problems in retrieving the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To save time, Mr. President, perhaps I could show the witness my copy, and when the other is located, we could change them around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps that is a good way of doing it. Might I just first have a look at it, if they do not come from the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it sufficient for the Defence to look at it on the ELMO, or would you like to see it prior to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am sorry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The original has been found, so perhaps Mr. Ierace could have that back.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It was on the Defence list, anyway, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, when the -- when you have an opportunity to look at the photograph, can you tell me if this appears to be the view that one would have if you were standing between the arterial road and the chapel and looking north? I don't suggest this photograph was taken during the war, but rather after the war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, it is clear that it was done after the war, and this can be seen by this building where the high representative is housed now. And this photograph was taken roughly in front of the entrance to the cemetery, not in front of the chapel, but in front of the entrance to the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now, in the foreground we see the arterial road, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And we see what appears to be a garage that has been elevated to road level. Was that there during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not see that from any position.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But you've told us that you knew the area extremely well and had since you were a child. Can you tell us, was that building there before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: By its appearance, I could say that it was, but I really don't see that I have to remember a garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Is it your evidence that you don't remember, but going on some holes in the bricks you think maybe it was damaged during the war; is that the situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, approximately how far to the left would this be from the chapel -- I'm sorry -- how far to the right would this be from the chapel having regard to your earlier answer that you think this photograph was taken from the entrance to the cemetery, rather than in front of the chapel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be some 50 metres away from the chapel, but from the position that I was in it is impossible to see this building.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you remember that you earlier indicated that the stairs, that is the entrance to the cemetery was in the middle of the red circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And that the front of the cemetery was approximately 100 metres, that boundary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And that the chapel was approximately 20 by 30 metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I suggest to you that when you put all those figures together, the distance between the entrance to the cemetery and the closest part of the chapel would have been significantly less than 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the entrance to the cemetery to the chapel?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, it's less than 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, from the position of the photographer there was a view of the intersection of Marijn Dvor, do you agree with that, whenever this photograph --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you see the intersection in the area of the centre of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: From the chapel would you expect there would --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
