utterances.text: The witness is now looking to -- without being asked to do so. If Mr. Ierace would like you to look at another photograph, he will ask you to do such. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please point to the intersection.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates an area slightly to the right of the centre of the photograph in the vicinity of what appears to be a patch of dark blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, from the chapel would you expect there would have been a clear view of the intersection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I ask the witness now be shown the second photograph, that is the same exhibit number ending in ERN 24-A. And perhaps the first photograph can be kept close by so the witness can look at both.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that what we appear to have here is a telephoto photograph of the Marijn Dvor intersection taken from the same position as where the first photograph was taken? And if you like, take your time and compare the two photographs to satisfy yourself that that is correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you please with the assistance of the usher -- I withdraw that. Looking at this photograph, yesterday you told us that in relation to the buildings to the right there was a wall. Do you remember saying that, that is --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you see the wall in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please point to -- I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am unable to recognise it here. This doesn't look to me to be that wall. Maybe this photograph was taken after the war, sufficiently later when the war, because of its damage and unfunctionality was pulled down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I don't want to mislead you, this photograph was certainly taken after the war, as was the earlier one. You pointed to in your answer to a wall that is white and has a number of cars parked along it. The wall is to the bottom of the photograph from the middle the right. Now, was that the position of the wall, approximately, that was there during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This wall should have had a different appearance before the war, and I show you now. Roughly from this position where we have the lamp post and along this line which is even longer, it extends beyond the framework of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness indicates from the lamp post which appears to the right of the blue area extending with his pointer from that position to the left, and then downwards to the bottom left-hand corner of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, from where the photographer was standing, the wall would not have impeded the view of the tramline, would it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And having regard to the height difference between the position where the wall was and the tram, I take it you would not expect the wall to impede a line of sight from the chapel to where the tram was, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please return to the other photograph and could you please point out the State Hospital.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates white high-rise building facing the position of the photographer halfway down the photograph and mid-way between the centre and the right hand margin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you expect -- I withdraw that. Were you able to see the State Hospital from where you were during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, would you please point to the executive buildings in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Executive Council building and this is the Assembly building, Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicated the two immediately adjoining high-rise buildings as the executive buildings and the lower building in front with horizontal white stripes indicating about five storeys or six storeys as the Executive Council building.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yesterday, in a different photograph you commented on the holes in the side of the executive building and said those holes were made by tank fire from Bosnian Serb forces in response to sniping; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were you sniped from those buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How do you know this sniper fire came from those buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is experience that is gained in wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you have any military experience before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So do you tell us that as an ordinary civilian, as a result of being under fire one develops the ability to detect the source of sniping fire, even over half a kilometre, is that what you tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just that, but there were also other means of detecting sniper positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But partly that? I don't dispute it. I simply want you to clarify.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why I say that there are also other means of determining the exact source of or origin of sniper activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP16, Mr. Ierace asked you now twice whether on the basis of your experience in the war you were able, even without having specific military training before the war, that on the basis of this experience that you were able to know or to identify where sniper fire came from, that you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can tell us if you want about the other sources, but this was the question. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, to the right of the executive we see another high-rise building of a similar height. Would you please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness does so, at the high-rise in the centre of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What building was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That building behind it of the same size and of the same appearance, we called it Moma and Uzeir. These are buildings used as business premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: To your personal knowledge, did it ever have a military purpose during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally am not aware of these buildings having been used to act against the units of the Army of Republika Srpska at the positions where I was stationed, but similarly actually both directions was visible. It was fire being opened from those buildings and from the Marshal Tito Barracks while the JNA was still located there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. So we are talking about in mid-1992, is that correct, early or mid-1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In your answer it was translated -- you were translated as saying "these buildings" but we only see one in the photograph in that position. Did you mean "this building" or "these buildings"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same buildings. A small part which you should be able to see here to the left, it is a little lighter it is the same one, the Marshal Tito Barracks is located here. So from the Marshal Tito Barracks you can see both buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates in relation to the position of Marshal Tito Barracks a complex halfway down the photograph and on the extreme left. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Ierace, we should clarify that the witness pointed at the darker high-rise building in the middle of the photograph that this building is hiding almost completely another one that is behind it from the point of view of the photographer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, you told us that the executive was shelled twice. When?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean that the men from the Republika Srpska Army shelled the Executive Council building on two occasions? Well, I can say that that was in the course of 1992 and 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, you said Executive Council. Do you mean the high-rise buildings or the low-rise white building? I am asking you about the high-rise building with the visible tank shell holes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When was that shelled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is the building you are referring to, I think it was towards the end of 1992 and the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When it was shelled, did that stop the sniping? To be clearer, was there sniping at any stage from that building after it was shelled in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So snipers were able to use the burnt-out building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In some ways I imagine it would have been even harder to see the snipers operating from the building in its burnt-out condition rather than its pristine condition, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So, sir, that wasn't the real reason it was shelled by Bosnian Serb forces, was it, to stop snipers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really judge that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, the building had symbolic significance, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the building of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Of which Republika Srpska did not want to be a part, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. This building was the building of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I am not referring to the Muslim side, but to the joint republic which was part of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Indeed. But didn't the -- wouldn't you tell us that the Serb community, the majority of the Serb community disagreed with what the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina did in 1992 in terms of declaring its independence from the former Yugoslavia; isn't that what you would say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally didn't speak about that, but this building has nothing to do with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I suggest to you that the building was hit and gutted because of its symbolic importance; do you agree or disagree or say you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with you. That building is a symbol of Sarajevo and of the Muslims and the Croats and of Serbs, as well. So it would not be right to accuse one side of having done this for political reasons. The shelling was directed against snipers and that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, the high-rise building, that is the one of the two that we can see at the intersection, was that gutted during the war, in the early stages of the war as a result of fire from the Bosnian Serb side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was translated to me as "destroyed" whereas you can see that this is not the case. It was damaged, but it -- not by the Army of Republika Srpska, but by the JNA. All the window panes were shattered in an exchange of fire between the two armies, the JNA which was in the Marshal Tito Barracks, and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time, or rather the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, may I ask you if you continue this line of questioning, perhaps you could please consider in what way this will assist the Chamber in making its determinations. I see that there is an exchange of, rather interpretation, of what happened --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your position is clear and I think the answers of the witness is clear as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Incidently in giving your answer you said that the fire was caused by the JNA, not the Bosnian-Serb Army, and yesterday you told us that the JNA withdrew. Sir, what was the name of the JNA Corps that was responsible for Sarajevo before the war? What part of the JNA was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, objection. Objection. The first thing that we request, if you think this is useful, this is someone who hasn't got any training or military -- or didn't do any military service, one should ask such a person how he could have had such knowledge. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, he came up with the answer without specifically being asked on it. You told us that the building you just indicated was damaged by the JNA, and Mr. Ierace asked you what part of the JNA was there before the war? What is the basis of your knowledge that this building was damaged by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the interest of saving time, that's not actually the point of the question. Rather the point is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that -- I do understand that I am not putting exactly the same question as you intended to do, but I would first see to clarify. How do you exactly know that it was the JNA that damaged that building or a part of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General knowledge of the situation in Yugoslavia before the war broke out, this territory was considered to be the territory of the Sarajevo Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but my question --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And part of these --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- How do you know that this building was damaged by the part of the JNA? Did you see it happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From where did you see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From my home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you see the source of fire of the bullets or shells that hit the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't believe there were any shells. There was -- fire was opened from rifles, that was visible. That's also characteristic of this war. Both sides --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- Used incendiary ammunition, so it was visible at all times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said "both sides"? That does not appear in the transcript. Did you say both sides used incendiary ammunition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was asking you where did you see the rifles and as I now understand, perhaps both sides, but where did you see the rifles that were firing at this building, when it was damaged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From that distance I couldn't see the rifles, but I saw fire being exchanged in both directions. So from the office buildings I am pointing to you and the Marshal Tito Barracks, which was located here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I understand your answer correctly if I say that you saw fire coming from both sides, and that although you couldn't see the rifles that you observed fire coming from the area of the Marshal Tito Barracks when this building was damaged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might the witness again have map -- the earlier map on the ELMO, the one he first saw, I think it is D1180 and might the witness be given a ruler, if someone has a ruler.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, first of all, would you place a dot in the middle of the chapel.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In the middle -- thank you very much. Would you now take the ruler and lay an edge of the ruler so that the red dot, the middle of the red dot 24 and the middle of the dot you just placed on the chapel are lined up.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you now take a blue pen and draw a line connecting, the red dot, the blue dot in the middle of the chapel and extend that same line very carefully down to the bottom of the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the tanks that fired on the executive, where were they when they hit the executive? That's in late 1993 and early -- I am sorry -- late 1992 and early 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At this location, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Would you please place a cross there and the letter "A" alongside the cross.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know how many tanks were involved on those two occasions? Was it one or more than one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now, I draw your attention back to the chapel on the map and where you placed the front line yesterday of the ABiH, it comes up across the arterial road, incorporates the chapel, and then moves easterly across the northern part of the cemetery to the eastern boundary; is that correct? That's correct, I think, do you agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Incidently, the eastern and western sides, were they approximately 300 metres long each, the eastern side and the western side of the cemetery, just approximately.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are referring to the walls of the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now, can you tell me this: If your forces -- I am sorry -- if the enemy forces controlled the chapel, such a significant position, it being the only building on that part of the confrontation line for the ABiH, do you know why your forces did not destroy it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason was the cultural significance they had.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I see. So did you ever fire at the chapel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were mortars used against the chapel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Shells were never used against the chapel; is that correct? Mortars shells, artillery shells, tank shells?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very beginning of the war, as far as I can remember, heavy -- a heavy weapon was used on one occasion in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, I suggest to you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of the chapel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I suggest to you there was a reason why the chapel wasn't destroyed. I suggest to you the reason is that your forces occupied it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very beginning of the war, I personally phoned the official, the Jewish official in Sarajevo at the time to tell him to do everything in the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina to ensure that the BH TO and later the BH Army leave. The Serbian forces and I, as neighbours in that building, I was never in that building from 1992 up until today. Not a single member nor a single member of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: There was no reason why the tank could not have continued up through your road and being a tank simply blasting the building, was there, technically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In technical terms, yes, but not in military terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In military terms you say that a building being the executive of the state was not an impediment to using tank fire to eliminate snipers, but a cemetery chapel was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not exactly what I said, but in principle I could agree with that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is time for a break. Mr. Ierace, do you have any idea how much time you would still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I may -- it is difficult for me to anticipate. I will be within the time taken by the Defence. I expect in the order of half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think taking into consideration interruptions, et cetera, et cetera, I think it would be fair to limit you to 20 minutes. That's -- I have on my list until now, two and a half hours. The Defence took approximately two hours to 40 and 45 minutes. There would be a bit more interruptions as the Prosecution was examining the witness. So if you could please try to finish in 20 minutes. We will adjourn until five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, would you please place the better "B" on the map alongside the circle indicating your position.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We have lost the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It appears again on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please place the better "B" alongside the circle indicating your position.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Having regard to the line that you drew earlier, we see that there is the same line of sight subject to obstacles as was enjoyed by the chapel of the intersection at Marijn Dvor, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on this map that is how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, I suggest to you that the difference in height between the chapel and the land where you were is in excess of 40 metres, in other words, the area where you and your fellow troops were positioned is at least 40 metres, not feet, metres higher than where the chapel was. Do you agree, disagree or do you say you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did your company -- I withdraw that. Did your forces have anti-aircraft artillery in the area in the vicinity of the cemetery between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only on one occasion, after which that heavy weapon was removed upon instructions from the French units that were just below the chapel of the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When was the artillery removed, the anti-aircraft artillery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It isn't artillery. It is an anti-aircraft machine-gun, and it was removed the same day it was brought there. And this happened at the beginning of 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: During 1994 I suggest to you there was an armed conflict between Aleksic and his troops on the one hand, and other Serb forces on the other hand. Do you agree or disagree or say you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you ever see forces from Serbia come to the vicinity of the cemetery in 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those men who came were not soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you aware that there was an incident at Markale market in early February 1994, yes or no, involving allegedly the death of dozens of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you say that it was before or after that date that UNPROFOR personnel were positioned at the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you mean after that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yesterday, when you were asked when they were positioned there, you said January, February or March 1994. I take it you are not sure when it was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after that event.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say you don't recollect how long it was after that event, whether it was one month, two months or three months, or even longer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very soon after that event.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you say that those UNPROFOR forces maintained a 24-hour observation post in the positions you marked on another map, I think four positions altogether.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When did you first have contact with an investigator or lawyer from the Defence team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in June this year.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Whenever it was that UNPROFOR observers were placed at the cemetery, did it strike you as odd that such a small place, such a small part of the confrontation line would warrant four separate teams of observers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that was logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I suggest to you that the State Hospital was regularly shelled with an anti-aircraft machine-gun, as you call it, between September 1992 and August 1994 from positions held by the Bosnian-Serb Army in the vicinity of the Jewish cemetery. Do you agree, disagree or say you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I suggest to you that around the 23rd, 24th or 25th of September, 1992, a tank or large artillery gun fired on the State Hospital from the vicinity of the Jewish cemetery. Do you agree, or disagree or say you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree because I see no reason why that would be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you mean by that that you are not aware of any military use to which the State Hospital was put in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From what I know and what was accepted as a general rule, the Military Hospital was abandoned in May 1992 and it was an empty building. It was not occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Who told you that? Or what sources of information do you rely upon for that point of view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army left Sarajevo in the course of May 1992, and that facility as a Military Hospital was the ownership and a part of the Yugoslav People's Army. And as they left with them went the personnel of that hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did your brigade, to your knowledge, have a platoon of snipers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that sniping screens were used in Grbavica to obstruct views. Did the erection of those sniping screens reduce the number of casualties of pedestrians, be they military or civilian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: To a high degree, it did reduce the number of victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You also told us yesterday, as I understood it, that you gave a copy of the report, the data on civilian deaths in part of Grbavica, to UNPROFOR. Who did you give it to in UNPROFOR and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't give the document to anyone, but I provided the information and there was a discussion about those casualties, and this could have been in the course of 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you aware of that data ever being provided to anyone in the public domain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to the international community nor to the public of a part of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Republika Srpska. It was not provided to anyone in the form of a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Who was it in UNPROFOR that you gave information to from that material in 1998 or 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that one of my duties was cooperation with the international community. So that people would contact me from the French units, the Italian units --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, I will interrupt you, we don't have much time. You did say, I provided the information and this could have been in the course of 1998 and 1999. Who did you give that information to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Who in UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Italian units.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was the person's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I do know he was a general.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Where was he stationed at the time that you gave this Italian general the information? Was it at Butmir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exact location of the Italian units and those zones of responsibility I am not sure of, but that gentleman came with an escort to the municipality of Novo Sarajevo and was of great assistance to that municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know where that documentation is now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably in the same place where it was until now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If required, would you be able to obtain it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I provided that data yesterday, I will personally do my best to obtain that document and make it -- put it at the disposal of both you and this Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You also told us yesterday that you saw the tank firing from Hum. Were you looking at the tank with binoculars or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no need to use binoculars.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was it about the tank that indicated to you that it was firing at that time? Was there smoke or a muzzle flash or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shell it fired destroyed an apartment in the immediate vicinity of the place where I was living with my family during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No. My question is: How do you know the shell came from that tank? What was it about the tank that indicated it was responsible for the firing? Specifically, could you see a muzzle flash?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you see a muzzle flash?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether you have heard these two names before: Jozo Andzic or Ferdo Dejanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Have you heard before the name Papic in relation to someone perhaps associated with Slavko Aleksic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A member of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was his rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was a regular soldier. He was not a professional soldier. He was just like me, like most of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was his relationship with Aleksic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As anybody else's, ordinary, cooperation in preserving the front lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Where was he positioned in late 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late 1994, Papic --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, in late 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even in late 1993, Papic was not located anywhere as a soldier because he had already been seriously injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown again map D1811.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, would you please take the pointer and place it on the middle of the three red circles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What is the street which is immediately south and indeed touching the red circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Ozrenska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please look carefully at the map. I appreciate the contour lines are not especially visible, and they take some concentration. Do you see on the map further south of the -- that same red circle, according to the contour lines one indicating a height of, I think, 600 metres? If so, would you please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that. You are now tracing that contour. Will you continue to trace that contour so that we can all see it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Please continue, as far as you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now, to the right, that is in between the middle red circle and the one on the far right, is there a hill with the elevation marked of 623 metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, the witness points to the number 623.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: As we move from that point towards the left, firstly, does that point 623 indicate a high point on the ridge line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please move further along the ridge to the left, very slowly, from 623.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And stopping when you next see -- when you see the next high point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness now stops at a point where there is a figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please read out that figure?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now, between that elevation of 630 and coming back to 623, is there another high point, one in between?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know of on the ground, the slopes decline and there is a vale there, actually on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: As translated that reads "a vale." What do you mean by a vale?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that the slopes -- the slope goes down in the opposite direction in relation to the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The light green line to the best of your knowledge in the area of Ozrenska Street, does that accurately depict the positions of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Though it is not possible to say with certainty, but I could accept it as a correct indication.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: According to your understanding, therefore, would -- as of the 11th of January, 1994, would the distance between the light green line and the line you drew yesterday be no-man's land?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't want to bother anyone, but I will need a few minutes for questions of translation and also the cross-examination of Mr. Ierace will require some re-examination on our part. So I think he has exceeded his time limit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I think that, unless it is for a break, I have been very often relatively liberal, even when I said five or seven minutes, it sometimes turns out to be nine or ten. And I think that I am perfectly able to do that myself. But, nevertheless, thank you for your assistance. I know that you need a couple of minutes. Mr. Ierace, apart from that, I was in the course of reminding you that the 20 minutes have elapsed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll only be another few minutes, I should think just a couple.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But just within three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you. Might I just check the last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Now, I suggest to you that the various positions indicated by red dots on this map with the exception of number 15 were visible from positions held by the Bosnian-Serb Army along this ridge. Do you agree, do you disagree or do you say that you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska were not in these two circles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am not asking you about the two circles. If you could listen carefully to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think that the witness wanted to answer and I think it is important that he be allowed to answer. He was familiar with the terrain and he should be allowed to answer and I also think that Mr. Ierace spoke rather loudly, raised his voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it would have been sufficient to say, "Mr. President, would you allow the witness to answer?" On my screen I see that the answer given was -- you were asked about the positions held by Bosnian-Serb Army along the ridge and you said: "First of all, the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska were not in these two circles." Did you want to add anything to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The separation or rather no-man's land between the two warring parties was not as small here because in that case the existence of the line itself would be called in question. As it is a ridge, it would not be logical, below the ridge to have the Army of Republika Srpska and in their immediate vicinity on flat ground or slightly below them to have the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So I am claiming that the Army of Republika Srpska had positions on the other side of the hill or the ridge because that is also logical from the military standpoint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are not talking about logics, but we are talking about facts. Sometimes facts are illogical. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, I would now like you to answer the question I asked you: Do you agree or disagree or say you don't know that those various red points except for 15 were visible from positions of the Bosnian-Serb Army in the area of Ozrenska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Points 7, 10 and 27 were certainly not visible. As for 20, I am not quite sure about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. For the parties --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There will be some questions from the Bench as well. So if the parties could please proceed as efficient as possible. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is there any need to cross-examine -- to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, I will do my best to comply with your advice.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, a moment ago you mentioned the existence of so-called incendiary bullets. Do you remember that, at least that is what we have in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you know what is the difference between so-called incendiary bullets and so-called tracer bullets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, the difference is small.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like to go back to your statement a moment ago with regard to the destruction of an apartment that was close to yours at the time. Do you remember that; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you know that that apartment was targeted by tank fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that it was a target at all. It was simply as the President said, it was a fact; it wasn't logic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I'd like to go back now to these exchanges of fire between the Tito Barracks and the building that you indicated as being dark and a high-rise building. To make things quite clear, can you give us an idea of the date when these exchanges of fire occurred, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in any event at the end of April or the beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, you told us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the witness was referring to 1992, yes? Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke to us about these high-rise building as being typical for fighting in built-up areas where snipers would position themselves. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect to these two buildings --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, in principle, please give me an answer in principle.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. That was an issue which came up in examination-in-chief the use of high-rise buildings as source of sniping fire, not cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I am going to rephrase and move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's not the same, but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: They spoke to you about the State Hospital. Was that a high-rise building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you stated a moment ago during the cross-examination that it was abandoned by its previous occupants, do you remember that, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. During the events that followed the depart of the previous occupants, was that building reused for any purpose whatsoever; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness has given clear evidence in cross-examination about the purpose of that building and its nonpurposes during the war. In view of that answer, this question has no relevance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the -- your question suggests something that contradicts the evidence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think there is a difference between occupying and using. I think that the witness -- may I ask the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First, look at what exactly the witness testified. And may I ask the usher to ask the witness to leave the courtroom for one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think, if I remember correctly, "nobody" was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think it was mentioned that the building was empty. But let's just have a look. It is page 76, I think. Yes, line 19. "From what I know and what was accepted as a general rule, the Military Hospital was abandoned in May 1992 and it was an empty building, it was not occupied."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the previous question and answer are also directly relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that there was no -- "do you mean by that that you are not aware of any military use to which the State Hospital was put in that period?" And the period was a few questions before was between September 1992 and August 1994. The evidence of the witness is perfectly clear that it was an empty building during that period, that there was no use to attack it. He did not limit it in time in whatever way and you are now suggesting in your question that it was re-used during this period of time, unless you are referring do a period of time after the time relevant of indictment and then, of course, the question of relevance comes up. Could you please escort the witness into the courtroom. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed, keep in mind the guidance we just gave you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, bearing in mind the answer that you gave with regard to the State Hospital, what we call the State Hospital, do you know, even if this is just occasional, do you know if this site could have occasionally been used --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in my respectful submission, that is blatantly contradictory to the ruling you just gave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will conclude. I will move on to another subject. I want to say how I wanted to formulate the question. This had to do with other things than what it was used for before. So being interrupted before I even finished my question, I just wanted to say what my question would have been and I think it would have been acceptable if it had been formulated in this manner. May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may put questions to the witness. You may not explain how you would have formulated the question if there would have been no objection. Put questions to the witness, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will put the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know whether any given moment in time during the events this building could have been used in any manner even if it had been in a punctual manner by anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will withdraw that question to save time. I will withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you remember the building, the tower of the Executive Council that was allegedly shelled; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In order to save time, we will work on the basis of our memory. But it is true to say that the lower part of that building appeared to have been less damaged than the higher parts?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The issue of damage to the building arose in examination-in-chief. There was nothing in cross-examination which related to there being more damage to the top, less damage to the bottom. This is a fresh issue in that sense, otherwise it relates to evidence in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I will explain why. But the witness should leave --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... And would the parties, please, it is the last 10 minutes of this week. I urged both parties not to intervene. It takes more time to have these discussions rather than to proceed. So the question to you was, Mr. DP16, whether the lower part of the building just mentioned appeared to have been less damaged than the higher parts or perhaps the other way around, if we put the question in a nonleading way. Which part, the higher part or the lower part would be more damaged, if there was any difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The floors in the lower part were less damaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why, very briefly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Visibility. The visibility of the first few floors, because the first floors were not that visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: From the town or from the hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general, from any position.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. A minute ago you spoke about the year 1993 as being a little calmer as far as the fighting is concerned. Can you tell us what you mean when you say this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the intensity of the exchanges of fire and the intensity of the fighting, whatever its form, was not as great in comparison to 1992 and 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, a minute ago you expressed your position with regard to the chapel. You drew the line of sight. Was the chapel an obstacle; yes or no? Was it an obstacle from your position with regards to the incidents that you saw in the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know this is leading, Mr. President. This is in order to save time. We have all used this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, a minute ago in exhibit 37795 [as interpreted] you saw the existence of a garage. My question is as follows: The Prosecution made you mark one or two impacts in the course of combat. Do you know, given the type of construction concerned, the type of construction that you saw in this image, do you know whether this building could have been easily destroyed, and I am referring to the garage, by any kind of weapon that the side had at the time of the conflict; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you please try to conclude because you needed a few more questions. The Chamber -- the Bench has some questions as well. You need some time for translation. The Chamber has some questions as well. It is Friday and we would like to conclude with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know. I will forget about the translation and continue with the questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke about a photograph and you mentioned the existence of a wall which had been partially destroyed along the tram track. Do you remember speaking about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact it is not along the tram station -- well, yes, in fact, yes, but more to the south.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That wasn't the evidence of the witness. It was given in chief and it was not that the wall was along the tram track.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it is -- I think that's what the witness corrected already. We are talking about the same wall you indicated before. Your question would be, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, exactly. The question is:

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were there also trees? Do you know anything about this? Were there any trees that were in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I am going to now ask my last question very quickly. A minute ago you spoke about when the Prosecution put questions to you, you spoke about the Mujahedin and about holy war, do you remember speaking about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't remember the mention of a holy war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has not -- it was not in translation, holy war, but I think it was translated as -- perhaps you could assist me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness spoke about a jihad, I think. I think that this is what I heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... Use the words he had. Yes. It was not translated as "holy war" as far as I remember, but...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, since you used the word "jihad" with regard to the Mujahedin. My question is, what do you know about the jihad since you spoke about this, in a couple of words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is what is translated as a holy war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, there was a religious dimension in this, and my question is as follows: Since you spoke about Chetniks a lot, was there a religious elements when the term "Chetnik" is used? Is there a religious element in it; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And finally this may be leading, but with your permission, have you ever heard about -- can I ask you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask this question with your permission? It has to do with the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know what your question will be --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, I am aware of the time. No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. The Judges might have some questions for you as well. First Judge Nieto-Navia has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I am going to read a question and an answer and after that I will ask you something. The question was, we were talking about the State Hospital: "Do you know by that that you are not aware of any military use to which the State Hospital was put in that period?" And the answer was: "Yes, from what I know and what was accepted as a general rule, the Military Hospital was abandoned in May 1992, and it was an empty building. It was not occupied." That was your answer, according to the English transcript. My question is whether your answer is applicable to the whole period between August 1992 and September 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: No more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi also has a question for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] I know that we are running out of time, but I have two brief questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First we will ask the interpreters whether we could finish it? It might take some perhaps 10 minutes, but then I hope we will be ready. Is that agreeable?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is no problem, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your kind cooperation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. My first question is as follows: It concerns the weapons of the unit commanded by Mr. Aleksic. Were these weapons the same ones as those that other battalions and regiments had or did they have different weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavko Aleksic's unit was in one battalion like the other companies, and we had the same weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it was a unit like the others? It just had a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My second question has to do with the height of your positions to the west of the Jewish cemetery. You were stationed there, you marked your positions on a map, and you were asked as follows: Were your positions higher than 40 metres, were they at an altitude which was 40 metres higher than the altitude of the chapel and your answer was no. Does that mean that your positions, your own positions or, that is to say, the Serb positions and those are the positions concerned and what is the altitude concerned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That answer meant that my position was lower down, but not the other positions of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but if I have understood you correctly, the layout of the terrain went upwards and there were two companies of yours at altitudes which were higher than the altitude that you were at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My company, which was the 3rd company, as I said, was in that position and it had several trenches which were at a higher altitude than the altitude of my trench. So, one company had several positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you perhaps give the altitude in metres? How many metres higher up was it in relation to the chapel, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My position wasn't more than 5 metres above the chapel at the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and the other positions of the other positions which were at a higher altitude?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One position was on a level with the chapel and two positions were higher than my position and the position of the chapel. Perhaps by 10 or 15 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Sir, my last question concerns -- Defence asked you a question, they asked whether from your position you were able to see the points marked on the map, if you remember, number 7, 10 and 27, et cetera, and you said that from point 27, if I am not mistaken, there was no view, it wasn't possible. Did you want to say from your position you yourself or your position, were you speaking in the name of -- on behalf of the troops of the army, were you speaking on behalf of the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The loophole was directed in such a way that those points couldn't be seen from any position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP16, I've got a few questions for you as well. You yesterday told us that you were informed about the Holiday Inn being used by snipers. You got this information from those who came to the -- to your side. When did they come and when did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the war people from Sarajevo of Serbian and Croatian nationality, moved to Grbavica, some stayed in the territory of Grbavica and some went to other parts of the world of their own free will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they tell you how they knew that sniping was originating from the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They saw that personally because they also had a form of a work obligation. They had to move around the town in spite of the possibility of military activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So they observed it from outside the building rather than from inside the building; is that understanding of your answer correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then my next question relates to the map number D -- I think it is the map of 18 and 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have got a different number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is the one. We should have been more precise. When did you for the first time see this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have an image. I don't know if anyone else has an image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It says "no signal." But perhaps you could already answer that first question, when did you for the first time see that map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You have told us before that your positions were near the Jewish cemetery. You pointed to that on another map. Were you able to travel more to the west? Did you ever go in that direction during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. There were the families of all people who lived in Grbavica usually, and they were in Grbavica, so it was possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please indicate how you travelled to the west on this map, if the streets appear when you -- or didn't you go that far? Please point at the route you would take to where your family would be. It is not necessary to indicate exactly where your family was but -- yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can't see where the family was, but from this position and going down this street, it was possible to move in a normal manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please start at the first red point again and tell us what route you took.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you started there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You go down this road, the Moravska road and the military line was here but I was able to move around in this part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We understand that you were able to move around also at the other side of the military line you have drawn.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You just told me I thought that -- could you please indicate -- put the pointer again at the point where you said that the military line was -- no, where the military line was. It was after you passed --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then you continue. Yes, and now you come there at a -- yes. Near to the second red circle there is more or less a -- yes, could you please keep your pointer there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is in my view, the third one, the middle one. The middle of the three.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there. There seems to be something like a fork, as you understand what I mean, that is two roads coming together where you said that you take the southerly one. What at that fork, at that junction of roads, what is the name of the streets there? What would be the name of the street that continues to the elevation point you just indicated by 623?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ozrenska Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you would, as you just indicated, you would follow the road where it is partially Ozrenska Street and then you would take the more southern part of it again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is a cross of what you have drawn as the lines held by the VRS Army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Did you also take the northern road? Could you please again point with your pointer to the middle red circle. There you see you just moved to the west and taking this southern road. The road that is slightly up north and goes in approximately the same western direction, did you ever take that road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please follow that road, although I do understand that you never went there, and stop at the next circle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there. Would you have ever been where that circle is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that you could not see all kind of places in the city from these red points. Is my understanding correct that you never went there during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there during the war, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the point you just pointing at, at this very moment, that red circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. To this location, but not to these places in the course of the war. In the course of the war, these places were no-man's land. And it wouldn't have been logical. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you didn't go there during the war. You didn't go there any more after the war; is that my correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I have another question for you: You were asked about the -- whether Mr. Aleksic had a criminal record and you responded by saying I am not a policeman, that you had no knowledge about the criminal record, if there was any of Mr. Aleksic. And you said I think, that he had never -- he was never proceeded against. Then, as far as the other members of the unit commanded by Mr. Aleksic was concerned, you said that these other members certainly would have no criminal records. Could you explain to me why you would not know, as explained to you not being a policeman, know about the criminal record of your neighbour where you would have precise knowledge of all the other members of the unit, whether they had criminal records?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slavko Aleksic -- the others -- the other members of Slavko Aleksic's unit, like Slavko Aleksic, they were my neighbours, and some of them were my friends, close friends, too. So according to my personal information, none of them had a police record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of any kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give me an idea of how many foreigners there were in that unit and how many locals, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: 80 per cent were locals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the total unit was how strong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 100 people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your testimony is, whether I understand you correctly, that of these 80 locals you are certain that they had no criminal records?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that I am sure, but maybe there is one or two that I don't know about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you ever investigate that or is it just on that you never heard of criminal records of these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The street I lived in is a relatively short street, and there are about 50 houses in the street. Most of the people lived in that small area, and that is something that would have been known for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much for your answers. This concludes your evidence in this court. I thank you very much for having come the far way from where you live and for having answered questions of all the parties and of the Bench. I wish that you have a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please escort the witness out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next Monday we will not be sitting. Next Tuesday we will sit in the afternoon on from a quarter past 2.00 and I think the first thing we then should do is to hear further information as to the maps. But I would like to limit that in time, that I think 15 minutes should be enough for both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would spend 15 minutes for both parties on the maps. So if you are preparing any information, make it as concise as possible so that the Chamber is informed and that it does not make unnecessary time. We will adjourn until next Tuesday quarter past 2.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 2.06 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 3rd day of December, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 24 25
